content.text:
**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

The agreement imposes no MFN obligation on us. Licensee's payment obligations are governed by a fixed tiered fee schedule (US$7.50 down to US$5.00 per US$1m traded), with no undertaking to give Licensor rates or terms no less favourable than those extended to any third party and no obligation to match third-party offers. Supplemental payments, support charges, and the general provisions are similarly silent.

The only third-party-comparison mechanic is Licensor's Right of First Refusal in Article XXII, which bites on a sale of assets or a merger of Licensee — a change-of-control right, not a commercial-terms MFN — and belongs under the assignment/change-of-control rules rather than this one.

Worth noting for the negotiation list, though not a deviation: the agreement also gives us no MFN in our favour, so there is nothing preventing Licensor from offering better per-million rates to other licensees. If pricing is reopened, an MFN in our favour would be a sensible upside ask, but its absence is not a redline under this rule.
